subject: [PATCH] mm: mglru: splice all generations when reparenting a memcg

reviews.author: Barry Song
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Barry Song noted that Kairui's previous patch (mm/mglru: reparent folios from all generations) already implemented the same code, and Shakeel's patch makes it necessary to make this change even earlier.

Reviewer Barry Song pointed out that the patch description does not clearly explain why moving all generations is necessary, and requested a more detailed explanation.
sentiment_signals: lack of clarity in patch description
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks very much, Shakeel! I saw Kairui has exactly the same code here:

[PATCH v4 14/17] mm/mglru: reparent folios from all generations
https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/20261016-mglru-fg-v4-14-2106750c0bfa@tencent.com/

somehow, Shakeel's patch makes us need the change earlier even before
mglru-fg lands?

---

Thanks,
Barry

reviews.author: Kairui Song
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that FG's folio_inc_lru_refs may cause a race between aging and lazy promotion, potentially landing a folio in a stall gen list, but agreed that this issue is not critical and can be addressed separately.

Reviewer Kairui Song agrees that the patch improves safety and cleanliness of the code
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks for looking into this!

FG needed that because FG's folio_inc_lru_refs is a generic MGLRU
lockless lazy promotion, it may cause race between aging & lazy
promotion, landing a folio in a stall gen list. This isn't a big
problem, the worst outcome is a hotness inversion, which happens
almost once in a million times.

And right as Shakeel pointed out the problem already exists for
reparenting and lazy promotion, so we can fix it first.

---

Landing this one first is totally fine by me. The code is actually
safer and cleaner, in my opinion, with this patch.

2026-11-11.patch_summary: This patch fixes a list_del corruption issue in the Linux kernel's memory management system (mm) by splicing all generations of MGLRU lists when reparenting a memcg (memory control group). The problem occurs when a memcg goes offline and its MGLRU lists are moved to the parent, but only certain generations are moved. This can lead to a folio being left on a freed memcg, causing a use-after-free error. To fix this, the patch moves all MAX_NR_GENS lists, not just those from min_seq to max_seq, ensuring that all folios are properly reparented and avoiding the corruption issue.

reviews.author: Kairui Song
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Kairui Song pointed out that the description of sort_folio() behavior in the patch is inaccurate, as MAX_NR_GENS - MIN_NR_GENS equals 2, and a stale gen can be outside the range [min_seq, max_seq].

Reviewer Kairui Song noted that this patch is similar to a previous commit for MGLRU-FG, which is a clean fix, but was surprised the problem was already reproducible.
reviews.raw_body:
"sort_folio() puts the folio on the list for max_seq + 1" seems not
very accurate as MAX_NR_GENS - MIN_NR_GENS == 2, could be any stale
gen outside [min_seq, max_seq], right?

The fix itself looks good.

---

As Barry mentioned this is basically the same code as a prepare commit
for MGLRU-FG, which is a fine and clean fix, I just didn't realize the
problem was already reproducible though.

Thanks!

Reviewed-by: Kairui Song <kasong@tencent.com>

reviews.author: Baolin Wang
reviews.summary: The reviewer found the patch comments unclear but agreed that the proposed solution fixes a problem where a folio's generation can fall outside its LRU vector range, causing it to be left behind on a freed memcg.
reviews.raw_body:
+1. The comments are not easy to understand. IIUC, the problem is that 
the folio's gen can fall outside lruvec->[min_seq, max_seq], potentially 
causing the folio to be left behind on a memcg that is about to be freed.

But, yes, the fix is correct. So,
Reviewed-by: Baolin Wang <baolin.wang@linux.alibaba.com>

reviews.author: Andrew Morton
reviews.summary: Andrew Morton noted that the patch was merged into the mm-hotfixes-stable branch and therefore dropped from the -mm tree, requesting it be re-submitted if necessary.
reviews.raw_body:
The quilt patch titled
     Subject: mm: mglru: splice all generations when reparenting a memcg
has been removed from the -mm tree.  Its filename was
     mm-mglru-splice-all-generations-when-reparenting-a-memcg.patch

This patch was dropped because it was merged into the mm-hotfixes-stable branch
of git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/akpm/mm

------------------------------------------------------
From: Shakeel Butt <shakeel.butt@linux.dev>
Subject: mm: mglru: splice all generations when reparenting a memcg
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:09:13 -0800

Noah reported list_del corruption on single-node hosts running 7.2.11,
which already has commit bf4ade7dbd76 ("memcg: keep folio's objcg same as
its node").  The bad pointer is an MGLRU list head in a freed
mem_cgroup_per_node:

  slab mem_cgroup_per_node start ff31bfa36a3c9e00 pointer offset 528 size 1920
  list_del corruption. next->prev should be ffacf881ccc70e08, but was ff31bfa36a3ca010. (next=ff31bfa36a3ca010)

When a memcg goes offline, __lru_gen_reparent_memcg() moves its MGLRU
lists to the parent.  It moves only the generations (gens) from min_seq to
max_seq, and it puts each list at the same index in the parent.

A folio's gen in folio->flags can be ahead of the list it is on.  In the
parent, the same index can stand for an older gen, so the folio's gen can
end up older than its list.  Once the parent's min_seq passes that gen,
sort_folio() puts the folio on the list for max_seq + 1, where it stays
until the next aging.

If the parent goes offline before that aging, the folio is not moved to
the grandparent.  It stays on the parent's list after the parent is freed,
and the next list_del() on it touches freed memory.  This needs two
cgroups on one branch to go offline one after the other, such as a
container and then its pod.

The parent always has MAX_NR_GENS gens at this point, so every index is
valid in it.  Move all MAX_NR_GENS lists, not only the gens from min_seq
to max_seq.

A reproducer that drives these steps through the lru_gen debugfs file gets
a KASAN use-after-free on the freed mem_cgroup_per_node without this
patch, and no report with it.

Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20261111000913.22943-1-shakeel.butt@linux.dev
Fixes: f304652609ea ("mm: vmscan: prepare for reparenting MGLRU folios")
Signed-off-by: Shakeel Butt <shakeel.butt@linux.dev>
Signed-off-by: Andrew Morton <akpm@linux-foundation.org>
Reported-by: Noah Feldt <noah@feldt.systems>
Closes: https://lore.kernel.org/all/20261110132853.71228-1-noah@feldt.systems/
Reviewed-by: Kairui Song <kasong@tencent.com>
Reviewed-by: Baolin Wang <baolin.wang@linux.alibaba.com>
Tested-by: Noah Feldt <noah@feldt.systems>
  Link: https://lore.kernel.org/20261115124954.7146-1-noah@feldt.systems
Reviewed-by: Barry Song <baohua@kernel.org>
Cc: Johannes Weiner <hannes@cmpxchg.org>
Cc: David Hildenbrand <david@kernel.org>
Cc: Qi Zheng <qi.zheng@linux.dev>
Cc: Kairui Song <ryncsn@gmail.com>
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>

 mm/vmscan.c |   12 +++++++++---
 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

--- a/mm/vmscan.c~mm-mglru-splice-all-generations-when-reparenting-a-memcg
+++ a/mm/vmscan.c
@@ -4752,19 +4752,25 @@ void max_lru_gen_memcg(struct mem_cgroup
  * The same generation has different meanings in the parent and child memcg,
  * so this compromise method will cause the LRU inversion problem. But as the
  * system runs, this problem will be fixed automatically.
+ *
+ * Move all MAX_NR_GENS lists, not only the gens from min_seq to max_seq.
+ * An earlier reparenting can leave a folio whose gen is older than the list
+ * it is on. Once min_seq passes that gen, sort_folio() puts the folio on the
+ * list for max_seq + 1, where it stays until the next aging. If that list
+ * were skipped, the folio would stay behind on a memcg that is about to be
+ * freed. The parent has MAX_NR_GENS gens here, so every index is valid in it.
  */
 static void __lru_gen_reparent_memcg(struct lruvec *child_lruvec, struct lruvec *parent_lruvec,
 				     int zone, int type)
 {
 	struct lru_gen_folio *child_lrugen, *parent_lrugen;
 	enum lru_list lru = type * LRU_INACTIVE_FILE;
-	int i;
+	int gen;
 
 	child_lrugen = &child_lruvec->lrugen;
 	parent_lrugen = &parent_lruvec->lrugen;
 
-	for (i = 0; i < get_nr_gens(child_lruvec, type); i++) {
-		int gen = lru_gen_from_seq(child_lrugen->max_seq - i);
+	for (gen = 0; gen < MAX_NR_GENS; gen++) {
 		long nr_pages = child_lrugen->nr_pages[gen][type][zone];
 		int child_lru_active = lru_gen_is_active(child_lruvec, gen) ? LRU_ACTIVE : 0;
 		int parent_lru_active = lru_gen_is_active(parent_lruvec, gen) ? LRU_ACTIVE : 0;
_

The problem occurs when a memcg goes offline and its MGLRU lists are moved to the parent, but only certain generations are moved. This can lead to a folio being left on a freed memcg, causing a use-after-free error. To fix this, the patch moves all MAX_NR_GENS lists, not just those from min_seq to max_seq, ensuring that all folios are properly reparented and avoiding the corruption issue.
